extracted.intended_audience: parties and attorneys participating in NRC adjudicatory proceedings (adjudicants, intervenors, and their counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing discovery, disclosures, depositions, interrogatories, document production, protective orders, and related pretrial procedures in Nuclear Regulatory Commission adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for examination and cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The individual has read any written testimony on which they intend to examine or cross-examine and any documents to be used or referred to in the course of the examination or cross-examination; the individual has prepared themselves to conduct a meaningful and expeditious examination or cross-examination, and has submitted a cross-examination plan in accordance with § 2.711(c). Examination or cross-examination conducted under this section must be limited to areas within the expertise of the individual conducting the examination or cross-examination; the party on behalf of whom this examination or cross-examination is conducted and their attorney is responsible for the conduct of examination or cross-examination by such individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirement to submit cross-examination plan per §2.711(c); limits testimony to witness's expertise; party and counsel are responsible for individuals they present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures — identity and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent otherwise stipulated or directed, a party other than the NRC staff shall, without awaiting a discovery request, provide the name and, if known, the address and telephone number of each individual likely to have discoverable information relevant to disputed issues alleged with particularity in the pleadings, identifying the subjects of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must identify subjects of information; applies to any individual 'likely to have discoverable information' relevant to disputed issues alleged with particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial disclosures — documents and tangible things
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of, or a description by category and location of, all documents, data compilations, and tangible things in the possession, custody, or control of the party that are relevant to disputed issues alleged with particularity in the pleadings. When any required document is publicly available from another source, a sufficient disclosure is the location, title and a page reference to the relevant item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may disclose by reference to public sources (e.g., NRC website or Public Document Room) with location/title/page reference instead of copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and frequency of initial disclosures and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stipulated or ordered, initial disclosures must be made within 45 days after issuance of a prehearing conference order following the initial prehearing conference specified in § 2.329. Disclosures are continuing; a disclosure update must be made every month after initial disclosures on a due date selected by the presiding officer, unless the parties agree otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party must make initial disclosures based on information reasonably available at the time; not excused because investigation incomplete or others have not disclosed. Disclosure updates exclude documents developed/obtained during the two weeks before the due date and must include documents not included in previous updates. Duty to update ends when the presiding officer issues a decision resolving the disputed issue or as otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of expert testimony — identity
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to initial disclosures, a party other than the NRC staff shall disclose to other parties the identity of any person who may be used at trial to present evidence under § 2.711.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is separate from general witness disclosure and applies to persons intended to present expert or trial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert witness written report contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in proceedings with pre-filed written testimony or as otherwise directed, the expert disclosure must be accompanied by a written report prepared and signed by the witness, containing: a complete statement of all opinions to be expressed and the basis and reasons therefor; the data or other information considered by the witness; any exhibits to be used as a summary or support for the opinions; the qualifications of the witness, including a list of all publications authored within the preceding ten years; and a listing of any other cases in which the witness has testified as an expert at trial or by deposition within the preceding four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must be signed by the witness; covers both opinions and supporting basis, plus qualifications and testimonial history—used to facilitate effective confrontation and evaluation of expert evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and sequencing for expert disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: These disclosures must be made at the times and in the sequence directed by the presiding officer, or absent direction, at least 90 days before the hearing commencement date. If intended solely to contradict/rebut another party's expert, disclosures must be made within 30 days after the other party's disclosure. Parties shall supplement these disclosures when required under paragraph (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow presiding officer's schedule; rebuttal experts have a shorter window; supplementation obligations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretrial disclosures — witness and exhibit identification
rubrics_metrics.description: A party other than the NRC staff shall provide: the name and, if not previously provided, the address and telephone number of each witness, separately identifying those expected to present and those who may be called; designation of witnesses whose testimony will be by deposition and, when available, a transcript of pertinent portions; and an appropriate identification of each document or other exhibit, including summaries of other evidence, separately identifying those expected to be offered and those which may be offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures inform trial planning and permit objections to admissibility; distinguishes expected vs. may-call witnesses and exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and waiver rules for pretrial disclosures and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise directed, pretrial disclosures must be made at least 30 days before the hearing at which the issue is presented. A party may object to admissibility of documents identified under paragraph (c); a list of those objections must be served and filed within 14 days after service of the disclosures, unless a different time is specified; objections not so disclosed are waived except objections under § 2.337(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely serve admissibility objections generally results in waiver, so parties must monitor disclosure schedules closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, signature, service, and filing of disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: All disclosures under paragraphs (a) through (c) must be made in writing, signed, served, and promptly filed with the presiding officer or the Commission unless otherwise directed by order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatures are required and disclosures must be timely filed; follow any case-specific orders altering form or timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementation duty for disclosures and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who has made a disclosure is under a duty to supplement or correct the disclosure to include information thereafter acquired if ordered or when the party learns that in some material respect the information disclosed is incomplete or incorrect and the additional/corrective information has not otherwise been made known to other parties. For expert reports, the duty extends to information in the report and information provided through expert deposition; additions/changes must be disclosed by the time § 2.704(c) disclosures are due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement per the disclosure update schedule; expert deposition changes must be reported in the pretrial disclosure window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards Information disclosure controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure under this section of documents and records including Safeguards Information referred to in Sections 147 and 181 of the Atomic Energy Act will be according to the provisions in § 2.705(c)(3) through (c)(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguards Information has special access, background check, and protective order procedures (see §2.705(c) entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized discovery methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may obtain discovery by one or more of: depositions upon oral examination or written interrogatories; interrogatories to parties; production of documents or things or permission to enter upon land for inspection; and requests for admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These methods are the standard toolkit for obtaining non-privileged, relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of discovery — relevance and non-privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may obtain discovery regarding any matter, not privileged, that is relevant to the subject matter involved in the proceeding, whether it relates to the claim or defense of any other party, including existence, description, nature, custody, condition, and location of books, documents, or other tangible things and identity/location of persons having knowledge of any discoverable matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery is broad but bounded by privilege and relevance; in construction permit/operating license proceedings, discovery begins only after the prehearing conference and is limited to matters in controversy identified in the prehearing order and generally not after the beginning of that prehearing conference except upon leave for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery not objectionable because evidence would be inadmissible
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not a ground for objection that the information sought will be inadmissible at the hearing if the information sought appears reasonably calculated to lead to the discovery of admissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery may legitimately seek leads to admissible evidence even if the material itself may later be ruled inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on the frequency, extent, and form of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may set limits on the number of depositions and interrogatories, and may limit the length of depositions and the number of requests. The presiding officer shall limit frequency or extent of discovery if they determine the discovery sought is unreasonably cumulative or duplicative, obtainable from another more convenient source, the party seeking discovery has had ample opportunity to obtain it, or the burden/expense outweighs likely benefit considering needs, parties' resources, importance of the issue, and importance of proposed discovery in resolving the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits are case-specific and balance proportionality factors (burden, cost, importance, resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery of trial preparation materials (work product)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may obtain discovery of documents and tangible things prepared in anticipation of or for the hearing by or for another party's representative only upon a showing that the party seeking discovery has substantial need of the materials and that the party is unable without undue hardship to obtain the substantial equivalent. In ordering discovery of such materials, the presiding officer shall protect against disclosure of the mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories of an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High protection for attorney work product; party must show substantial need and undue hardship to overcome protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming privilege or protection for withheld materials
rubrics_metrics.description: When a party withholds information by claiming privilege or trial preparation protection, the party shall make the claim expressly and describe the nature of the documents, communications, or things not produced in a manner that, without revealing privileged information, will enable other parties to assess applicability of the privilege or protection. Identification must be made within the time provided for disclosure unless otherwise extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privilege assertions must be explicit and sufficiently descriptive (often via privilege log) to allow evaluation without waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible subject matter of interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrogatories may seek to elicit factual information reasonably related to a party's position in the proceeding, including data used, assumptions made, and analyses performed. Interrogatories may not be addressed to, or require: reasons for not using alternative data/assumptions/analyses not relied on; or performance of additional research or analytical work beyond that needed to support the party's position on any matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories probe factual bases and analytic inputs but cannot force new research or hypothetical justification for unchosen alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders — scope and available protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon motion (with certification of good-faith conferral) and for good cause, the presiding officer may make orders to protect a party/person from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, or undue burden/expense, including: that discovery not be had; discovery be had only on specified terms/conditions; discovery be had by a different method; certain matters not be inquired into or scope limited; discovery conducted with only designated persons present; trade secrets/confidential info be not disclosed or disclosed only in a designated way; or that studies and evaluations not be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective orders are flexible and can tailor access, confidentiality, locations, presence, and method to protect interests; movant must certify conferral attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer may order discovery despite denied protective motion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a motion for a protective order is denied in whole or part, the presiding officer may, on such terms and conditions as are just, order that any party or person provide or permit discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial of protection can be accompanied by conditional disclosure terms to mitigate harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards Information — access and background checks
rubrics_metrics.description: For documents and records including Safeguards Information, the presiding officer may order disclosure only if: the individual seeking access has the requisite 'need to know'; the individual has undergone an FBI criminal history records check (unless exempt) by submitting fingerprints and following procedures; and the NRC Office of Administration has found the individual trustworthy and reliable based on a background check (unless exempt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to Safeguards Information involves fingerprinting, criminal-history checks, background review procedures, and potential review of adverse determinations by a designated officer; additional protective terms may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving safeguards while minimizing procedural impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may prescribe additional procedures to effectively safeguard and prevent disclosure of Safeguards Information to unauthorized persons with minimum impairment of the procedural rights which would be available if Safeguards Information were not involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balancing protection of sensitive info with preservation of parties' procedural rights is required; sanctions (civil/criminal) may apply for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence and timing constraints on seeking discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when authorized or by order or agreement, a party may not seek discovery from any source before the parties have met and conferred as required by paragraph (f), nor may a party seek discovery after the time limit established in the proceeding for the conclusion of discovery. Methods may be used in any sequence and one party's discovery does not delay others unless the presiding officer orders otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must complete the required meet-and-confer and respect the schedule for the close of discovery; sequencing is flexible absent order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to supplement discovery responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who responded to a discovery request is under a duty to supplement or correct the response to include information thereafter acquired if ordered or within a reasonable time after the party learns that the response is materially incomplete or incorrect, and the additional/corrective info has not otherwise been made known to other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing duty to correct or add to prior answers—timeliness required once new material info is learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet-and-confer and development of a proposed discovery plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties shall, as soon as practicable and no more than 30 days after issuance of a prehearing conference order following the initial prehearing conference, meet to discuss the nature/basis of claims and defenses, possibilities for settlement or resolution, make/arrange required disclosures, and develop a proposed discovery plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must cooperate early to plan discovery and attempt settlement; meeting is a precondition to some discovery actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the discovery plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must indicate parties' views/proposals concerning: changes to timing/form/requirement for disclosures under §2.704 (including statement when §2.704(a)(1) disclosures were or will be made); subjects on which discovery may be needed, when discovery should be completed, and whether discovery should be phased or limited to particular issues; what changes should be made in the limitations on discovery imposed under these rules and what other limitations should be imposed; and any other orders that should be entered by the presiding officer under paragraph (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery plan should be substantive and propose concrete scheduling, scope, and limitation modifications to facilitate efficient discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to attend planning meeting and file plan report
rubrics_metrics.description: The attorneys of record and all unrepresented parties that have appeared are jointly responsible for arranging and being present or represented at the meeting, for attempting in good faith to agree on the proposed discovery plan, and for submitting to the presiding officer within 10 days after the meeting a written report outlining the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint responsibility imposes duty on counsel and pro se parties to cooperate in good faith; written report is mandatory and timely (10 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing certifications for disclosures, requests, responses, and objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Every disclosure must be signed by at least one attorney of record (with address) or signed by an unrepresented party (with address). Signature constitutes a certification that to the best of the signer's knowledge, information, and belief, formed after reasonable inquiry, the disclosure is complete and correct. Every discovery request, response, or objection by a party represented by an attorney must be signed similarly; the signature certifies that the request/response/objection is consistent with the rules and warranted by existing law or a good faith argument to change the law; not interposed for an improper purpose; and not unreasonable or unduly burdensome given the needs of the case, discovery already had, amount in controversy, and importance of the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsigned filings must be stricken unless promptly signed; violations can trigger sanctions including termination of participation in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to compel discovery — timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deponent or party fails to respond or objects to a request, the requesting party may move the presiding officer within 10 days after the date of the response or after failure to respond for an order compelling response or inspection. The motion must set forth the nature of the questions or the request, the response or objection, arguments in support, and be accompanied by a certification that the movant conferred or attempted in good faith to resolve the dispute. An evasive or incomplete answer will be treated as a failure to answer. Failure to answer is not excused on ground discovery is objectionable unless a protective order has been applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Movant must document conferral attempts; courts treat evasive answers as non-responses; protective order applications may affect remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer discretion on motions to compel — protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: In ruling on a motion made under this section, the presiding officer may issue a protective order under paragraph (c) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies on motions to compel can include conditional disclosure subject to protective safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent subpoenas and scope exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not preclude an independent request for issuance of a subpoena directed to a person not a party for production of documents and things. The section does not apply to requests for testimony or interrogatories of the NRC staff under §2.709(a), or the production of NRC documents under §§2.709(b) or 2.390, except for paragraphs (c) and (e) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoena power remains available for non-parties; special rules apply for discovery from NRC staff and NRC documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions — notice and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party desiring to take testimony by deposition shall, without leave, give reasonable written notice to every other party, the person to be examined and the presiding officer of time/place; name and address of person (or description if name unknown); matters upon which each person will be examined; and the name/description/address of the officer before whom the deposition is to be taken. Within the U.S., depositions may be before any officer authorized to administer oaths; outside the U.S., before consular officers or designated persons. Before questioning, the deponent shall be sworn/affirmed; examination and cross-examination proceed as at a hearing; each question must be recorded and answer taken down in witness's words; objections must be noted in short form without arguments; the officer must not decide competency/materiality/relevancy but record evidence subject to objection; objections not made before the officer will not be considered waived unless the ground could have been obviated if presented then.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositions replicate hearing procedures; proper notice and sworn transcript are required; objections handled by short-form notation and preserved for later rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions — transcription, signature, certification, and docketing
rubrics_metrics.description: When testimony is fully transcribed, the deposition must be submitted to the deponent for examination and signature unless ill, cannot be found, or refuses to sign; the officer shall certify the deposition or, if unsigned, certify reasons for failure to sign. The deposing party shall promptly transmit an electronic copy of the deposition to the Secretary of the Commission for entry into the electronic docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transcripts should be circulated for signature; the officer certifies; e-copy must be promptly sent for docketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions on written interrogatories — service and cross-interrogatories
rubrics_metrics.description: Where deposition is on written interrogatories, the party taking the deposition shall serve a copy of the interrogatories (numbered) on every other party with notice stating the name and address of the person to answer and the officer before whom they are to be taken. Within 10 days after service, any other party may serve cross-interrogatories. The interrogatories, cross-interrogatories, and answers must be recorded and signed and certified as in oral depositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism for written-question depositions with a 10-day cross-interrogatory window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and use of depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposition will not become part of the record in the hearing unless received in evidence. If only part of a deposition is offered, any other party may introduce other parts. A party does not make a person its own witness for any purpose by taking their deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking a deposition does not automatically bind the deponent as that party's witness; admissibility determined at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and representation at depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: A deponent and the officer taking a deposition are entitled to the same fees as are paid for like services in the U.S. district courts; fees must be paid by the party at whose instance the deposition is taken. The witness may be accompanied, represented, and advised by legal counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost allocation follows federal court analog; parties may have counsel present with deponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions of NRC personnel are governed separately
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions for depositions in paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(9) are not applicable to NRC personnel. Testimony of NRC personnel by oral examination and written interrogatories addressed to NRC personnel are subject to the provisions of § 2.709.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special handling and procedures apply when seeking testimony or interrogatories from NRC staff (see §2.709).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories — service, form, and response time
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may serve upon any other party (other than the NRC staff) written interrogatories to be answered in writing by the party served, or if a corporation/partnership/association, by any officer or agent with available information. A copy of the interrogatories, answers, and related pleadings must be filed with the Secretary and served on the presiding officer and all parties. Each interrogatory must be answered separately and fully in writing under oath or affirmation, unless objected to with reasons stated. Answers must be signed and objections by the attorney. The party served shall serve answers and objections upon all parties within 14 days after service of the interrogatories, or within such period as the presiding officer allows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatory answers are under oath, must be timely (14 days default), and are filed and served on all parties and the Secretary; objections replace answers when appropriate and must state grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for production — scope, specificity, and response time
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may serve a request to produce and permit inspection/copying of designated documents or to permit entry upon designated land/property for inspection/testing within the scope of §2.704 and in the possession/custody/control of the party served. The request may be served on any party without leave and, except as otherwise provided in §2.704, after the proceeding is set for hearing. The request must identify items individually or by category and describe each with reasonable particularity, and specify a reasonable time, place, and manner for inspection. The party served shall serve a written response within 30 days stating whether inspection will be permitted as requested, or stating reasons for objection and specifying parts objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be reasonably particular; 30-day response default; where NRC records are sought, §§2.709 and 2.390 apply instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for admission — form, deemed admission, and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time after its answer, a party may file a written request for admission of genuineness/authenticity of any relevant document or truth of any specified relevant matter of fact. A copy of the document must be delivered with the request unless previously furnished. Each requested admission is considered made unless, within a time designated by the presiding officer and not less than 10 days after service, the party serves either a sworn statement denying specifically the relevant matters or written objections on grounds privileged/irrelevant/improper. Answers on matters with objections may be deferred until objections determined. If objections to part of a request are made, the remainder must be answered within the time designated. Admissions obtained may be used in evidence to the same extent and subject to the same objections as other admissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule treats unlanswered admission requests as admitted; parties must timely answer or object (≥10 days) to avoid deemed admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery against NRC staff — availability of staff witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: In a proceeding in which the NRC staff is a party, the NRC staff will make available one or more witnesses, designated by the Executive Director for Operations or a delegee, for oral examination at the hearing or on deposition regarding any matter, not privileged, that is relevant. Attendance/testimony of the Commissioners and named NRC personnel may not be required by presiding officer, subpoena or otherwise; however, the presiding officer may, upon a showing of exceptional circumstances (e.g., a named employee has direct personal knowledge of a material fact not known to designated witnesses), require attendance and testimony of named NRC personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery from NRC staff is handled centrally; parties may need to show exceptional circumstances to require testimony from specific named NRC employees.
